clue.text: A sweet girl — shut the kid 0 out

indicators.note: out here means wrongly arranged or disordered, so the four words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovely girl tells someone to keep the child outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like praise for the girl, but 'A sweet' is the definition. 'out' rearranges GIRL SHUT THE KID into the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gel confection dusted with icing sugar, a classic sugary treat.

clue.text: Standard for man after marriage

indicators.note: after places the word for man behind the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union
Jack is a generic name for a man, as in 'every man jack'

explanation.surface: Asks what is the usual thing for a man once wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Country in which king meets singer

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Enya is the Irish singer

explanation.surface: A nation where a monarch encounters a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: An East African nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Fur with bluish green lining, not safe from thieves

indicators.note: lining means one piece sits inside the other, as a lining sits within a fur coat

parts.note: sable is a valuable fur
teal is a bluish green colour

explanation.surface: A fur coat with a teal lining that is at risk of being stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to theft is liable to be taken by robbers.

clue.text: Architectural style of Harewood or Ickworth

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the names that follow

explanation.surface: Asks which building style belongs to two English country houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Harewood and Ickworth are English stately homes; the answer runs across 'HarewooD OR ICkworth'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of columns, so a style of building.

clue.text: An ecu with gold pieces in a region of France

indicators.note: in pieces means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old French coin with bits of gold found in a French province.
explanation.walkthrough: The ecu was an old French coin, which nudges the solver toward France; 'pieces' breaks up AN ECU and GOLD together.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic province in southern France, so a French region.

clue.text: Pained utterance from Greek on a cross

indicators.note: cross means angry or put out, so the two little words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Greek crucified on a cross cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' seems a noun for crucifixion but is an adjective meaning annoyed, signalling ON A rearranged to OAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A low moan of suffering is a sound made when hurt.

clue.text: Drunkard turns to observe drunkard

indicators.note: turns means the word for drunkard is read the other way round

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
to spot is to observe

explanation.surface: A drunk switches to watching another drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' sends SOT backwards to TOS; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a heavy drinker, synonym for a boozer.

clue.text: Set up to continue transporting by water-it's just a short distance

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the phrase is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: to raft on is to keep carrying goods on a raft

explanation.surface: Arranging to keep shipping goods by boat since it is only a little way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' in this down clue turns RAFT ON upwards into the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Close by: a phrase meaning only a little way off.

clue.text: Hunter taking back black French duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: back means the French word is written in reverse

parts.note: noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A hunter returning with a black French duck he has shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the hunter's quarry, but it is the cricket score of nought; 'taking' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation.

clue.text: Wrong, or sure one is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters of the three words are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is wrong, or whether one is certain it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' appears twice: first as the definition, then in 'is wrong' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken or incorrect, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Pigeon enthusiast with dog

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A bird lover who keeps a pigeon and a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb here, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of domestic pigeon with a spread, fan-like tail.

clue.text: Having finally risen, milk can turn violently

indicators.note: having finally places the word for risen at the end, after the milk can

parts.note: a churn is a large milk can
up means risen

explanation.surface: A milk can that has risen gets turned over violently.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or agitate the ground or water, as a vehicle does with mud.

clue.text: Prepare study on the fourth of July

parts.note: to read is to study, as at university

indicators.note: the fourth of points to the fourth letter of July rather than the US holiday

explanation.surface: Get ready for Independence Day by studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fourth of July' suggests the American holiday but means the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something fit for use, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Shout now if ordering tuna

parts.note: to yell is to shout

indicators.note: ordering means putting into a new order, so the two short words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a restaurant told to call out now if they want tuna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' sounds like a restaurant order but rearranges NOW IF to OWFIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of tuna with yellow fins.

clue.text: Actors with markedly regional accents for radio or TV programme

parts.note: a broad accent is a strongly regional one
the cast is the group of actors

explanation.surface: Performers with strong local accents chosen for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission on air, a single show sent out to listeners or viewers.

clue.text: Be more than unconscious with anaesthetic

parts.note: out means knocked out, unconscious
an anaesthetic is something that numbs, a numb-er

explanation.surface: Being knocked out cold by an anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anaesthetic' is read as NUMB-ER, a thing that numbs, not the word for a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in count, being greater in quantity.

clue.text: Tempo for musicians as well as social worker in love

parts.note: and means as well as
an ant is a social insect and a worker
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A musical tempo, plus a social worker who has fallen in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a care professional but is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for a pace slightly quicker than andante.

clue.text: Be fond of untruths Tory leader makes most plausible

parts.note: to like is to be fond of
lies are untruths

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: Enjoying the falsehoods a Conservative chief tells as believable.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of probable: the best-supported and most credible.

clue.text: A flower to throw an essayist

parts.note: to lob is to throw
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Tossing a flower at a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with small blue or purple blooms.

clue.text: Wood clutched by Grace Darling

indicators.note: clutched by means the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A piece of timber held by Grace Darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling was a Victorian heroine who rowed out to rescue shipwrecked sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer, and its fragrant timber.

clue.text: Wood enclosed by railway without forethought

indicators.note: enclosed by means the tree goes inside the abbreviation for railway

parts.note: ash is a type of wood

explanation.surface: Timber fenced in by the railway, done carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impetuously, without considering the consequences.

clue.text: A graduate favours monkeys

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
boons are favours

explanation.surface: A university graduate who likes monkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Large ground-dwelling primates of Africa and Arabia.

clue.text: A high-ranking Muslim lady in Belgium left one out

indicators.note: out means the two letters are removed from the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A noble Muslim woman in Belgium leaves one person behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L and I from BELGIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia.

clue.text: Former rulers not affected by revolution

indicators.note: not affected by revolution says the letters read the same when turned backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Past monarchs who survived uprisings unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests the Iranian uprising that toppled the last one, but means turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian kings, the monarchs of Iran until 1979.

clue.text: Nymphs or nymphets first appearing in lingerie

indicators.note: appearing in puts the initial letter inside the underwear word

parts.note: undies are lingerie

indicators.note: first points to the initial letter of nymphets

explanation.surface: Young girls showing up in underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Water spirits of folklore, female elementals.

clue.text: Underground deputy head pops up to make first appearance

indicators.note: pops up in a down clue means the pieces read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway

indicators.note: head means the first letter of deputy

explanation.surface: A deputy chief emerges from the Underground to show their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pops up' turns TUBE plus D upward, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear for the first time, as a performer or product does.

clue.text: Roast building blocks. Flamboyant? Not half!

parts.note: Lego is the toy building blocks

indicators.note: not half here means take only half of the word, its first five letters

explanation.surface: A roast built from toy bricks; showy? Very much so!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it takes the first half of FLAMBOYANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat cooked in the oven, a classic Sunday dish.

clue.text: Fab fish

definitions.meaning: British slang for great or brilliant
a European flatfish related to the turbot

explanation.surface: Excellent seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for wonderful, and also the name of a flatfish similar to turbot.

clue.text: Government tempered its dominant air

indicators.note: tempered means modified or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Government moderated its domineering manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruling body or regime in office, as in the US usage.
